extracted.intended_audience: public relations and communications measurement professionals; PR practitioners and organizations seeking guidance on measuring PR/communications effectiveness
extracted.subtask_description: A set of industry guidelines (the Barcelona Principles) for planning, measuring, and evaluating public relations and communications campaigns, updated across 2010, 2015 (2.0) and 2020 (3.0). Useful for practitioners designing measurement frameworks and assessing PR campaign effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of goal setting and measurement (2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of goal setting and measurement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle stresses that setting goals and measuring against them is fundamental to assessing PR work. (Original 2010 wording — foundational requirement for planning and assessment.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure effects on outcomes vs outputs (2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measuring the effect on outcomes is preferred to measuring outputs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes prioritizing outcome-based measurement (changes in awareness, attitudes, behaviors, business results) rather than simple outputs (e.g., number of press releases, hits, impressions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure effect on business results where possible (2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect on business results can and should be measured where possible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages linking communications measurement to business performance indicators when feasible, to demonstrate impact on organizational goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media measurement requires quantity and quality (2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Media measurements requires quantity and quality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement should capture both the volume/scale (quantity) and the characteristics/valuation (quality) of coverage or media attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: AVEs are not the value of Public Relations (2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: AVEs are not the value of Public Relations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejects Advertising Value Equivalencies as a valid proxy for PR value; AVEs should not be used as the primary measure of communications worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media can and should be measured (2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social Media can and should be measured
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts that social media measurement is possible and necessary, and should be incorporated into PR measurement frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and replicability are paramount (2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency and replicability are paramount to sound measurement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement approaches should be open, reproducible, and defensible so results can be trusted and repeated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal setting and measurement are fundamental (2.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal setting and measurement are fundamental to communication and public relations:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Use a holistic approach that includes traditional and social media; be aware of changing variables. Make goals qualitative and quantitative and integrate SMART criteria evaluation across all channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure communication outcomes recommended over outputs (2.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measuring communication outcomes is recommended versus only measuring outputs:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Apply standards and best practices in target audience research to focus measurement on real communication outcomes rather than only on outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on organizational performance should be measured where possible (2.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect on organizational performance can and should be measured where possible:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Demand models to evaluate impact on target audiences and use survey research and business metrics (e.g., profitability, customer quality, revenue, market share, customer retention) to link communication work to organisational performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement requires both qualitative and quantitative methods (2.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement and evaluation require both qualitative and quantitative methods:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Measure impressions among stakeholders and target audiences and assess quality of media coverage. Capture positive, negative, and neutral progress — not only measures of success. Use mixed methods to produce richer insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: AVEs are not the value of communication (2.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: AVEs are not the value of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Instead use negotiated advertising rates relevant to the client, consider quality of coverage, and account for the physical space or time of coverage related to the portion that is relevant — avoid simplistic AVE calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media should be measured consistently with other channels (2.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media can and should be measured consistently with other media channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Focus measurement on engagement, 'conversation' and 'communities', not just 'coverage' or vanity metrics. Integrate social metrics into broader measurement frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement should be transparent, consistent and valid (2.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement and evaluation should be transparent, consistent and valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Ensure integrity, honesty, openness and ethical practices. Recognize potential biasing effects in the research itself or in the broader societal context; use consistent, valid methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting goals is an absolute prerequisite (3.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting goals is an absolute prerequisite to communications planning, measurement, and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reaffirms that goals must be established before planning and measurement; goals underpin what and how you measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify outputs, outcomes, and potential impact (3.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement and evaluation should identify outputs, outcomes, and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement frameworks should distinguish immediate outputs, subsequent outcomes, and longer-term potential impacts to provide clarity about levels of effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify outcomes and impact for stakeholders, society, and organization (3.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes and impact should be identified for stakeholders, society, and the organization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadens the focus beyond organizational metrics to include stakeholder and societal impacts when appropriate; encourages inclusive thinking about who is affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include both qualitative and quantitative analysis (3.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication measurement and evaluation should include both qualitative and quantitative analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restates the need for mixed methods to generate robust evaluation and insight, combining numeric indicators with qualitative understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: AVEs are not the value of communication (3.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: AVEs are not the value of communication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continues the explicit rejection of AVEs as a value metric; the principle remains central across versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic measurement includes all relevant online and offline channels (3.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Holistic communication measurement and evaluation includes all relevant online and offline channels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates for integrating measurement across channels (digital, social, traditional) to form a comprehensive view of communications performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement rooted in integrity and transparency to drive learning (3.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication measurement and evaluation are rooted in integrity and transparency to drive learning and insights
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises ethical, transparent approaches that enable learning and continuous improvement rather than only defensive proof of value; links measurement to insight generation.
